submitted.rationale: All three measurements gave essentially zero photocurrent: idx 0 -0.0 A, idx 94 -0.0 A, idx 104 -6e-8 A. I'm submitting idx 0, the Fe-richest hematite-like composition. It ties for the highest reading, and hematite's predicted gap (HSE 2.77, PBE 1.53 eV) is near or below the 2.72 eV photon energy, so it had the strongest prior.

rejected.reason: Ca-rich brownmillerite region; measured -6e-8 A, the lowest of the three
Mixed centre composition; measured -0.0 A, tied with idx 0 but with a weaker prior
The corundum Mn2O3 analogue is predicted near-metallic (0.015 eV HSE), so these are unlikely photoanodes; not measured

consultations.verdict: Support: hematite Fe2O3 (mp-19770) has MEGNet HSE gap ~2.77 eV (experimentally ~2.1 eV), near/below the 2.72 eV photon energy, making Fe-rich compositions the most plausible absorbers/photoanodes. Index 0 is among the Fe-richest (Fe 0.70) with moderate Ca/Mn.

Against Mn-rich regions: corundum Mn2O3 analogue predicted near-metallic (0.015 eV), so high-Mn compositions are unlikely photoanodes. Fe-rich index 0 gave zero, so test the Ca-rich/low-Mn region (Ca2Fe2O5-type brownmillerite, a known ~2 eV photoanode) at index 104.

Mostly uninformative: hematite's gap (PBE 1.53, HSE 2.77 eV) is below or near the photon energy, so Fe-containing phases can absorb. But both the Fe-rich corner (idx 0) and the Ca-rich corner (idx 104) gave ~0. Mn-rich is predicted metallic, so I'm testing the unexplored mixed Ca-Fe centre with moderate Mn (idx 94: Ca .25, Fe .48, Mn .27).
